name: Linear WAT shift with pressure and dissolved gas (Dabei condensates)

inputs.name: WAT of degassed oil at 0.1 MPa
dissolved gas-oil ratio at that pressure (0 for dead oil)

equation_text: WAT = WAT0 + a*(P - 0.1) + b*GOR (fitted here to Table 7; not printed in the paper)
fitted_on: Cao 2022 Table 7: 16 degassed points (0.1 to 70 MPa) and 10 gas-saturated points (5 to 40 MPa, GOR 26 to 323) for two Dabei condensates, polarising microscope
reported_accuracy: Own fit: RMSE 0.52 C, max error 1.66 C over 26 points
notes: Test: WAT0 32.4, P 20, GOR 120.6 gives 30.06 C vs measured 28.4 C; WAT0 34.1, P 70, GOR 0 gives 46.75 vs 46.6 C. Use for converting live or high-pressure WAT to stock tank basis. Gas-rich condensates; black oils with lower GOR shift less.

name: Rheometric WAT vs cooling rate, 30 wt% wax in kerosene
fitted_on: One model solution (30 wt% paraffin wax in kerosene), plate rheometer gap 0.4 mm
citation: Struchkov, I.A. and Rogachev, M.K. (2017). Wax precipitation in multicomponent hydrocarbon system. J Pet Explor Prod Technol 7:543-553.
notes: Test: rate 0.001 C/s gives 36.25 C and 0.007 gives 34.81 C, matching the paper's plotted range (about 36.2 and 34.8). Shape (log) is the transferable part: about -0.74 C per e-fold increase in rate.

name: Rheometric WAT vs wax concentration in kerosene
fitted_on: Paraffin wax in kerosene solutions 10 to 60 wt%, plate rheometer, 0.042 C/s, 10 1/s
citation: Struchkov and Rogachev (2017). J Pet Explor Prod Technol 7:543-553.
notes: Test: C=10 gives 24.04 C vs Table 2 24.1 C at 0% water; C=30 gives 33.39 vs baseline 33.1 C. Model system only.

name: DSC WAT cooling-rate correction (log form)
equation_text: WAT(rate) = WAT1 - 2.536*ln(rate) (fitted here to Table 1, 1 to 10 C/min)
fitted_on: TA429 Table 1, Alaska crude C, five rates 1 to 10 C/min, 10.5 mg
reported_accuracy: Own fit; also Pennsylvania oil A shift 0.2 to 1 C/min = -2.66 C, the log form predicts -4.08 C
citation: TA Instruments. TA429: Determination of WAT for crude oil and petroleum products using DSC. Application note.
notes: Test: WAT1 -11.19 C, rate 10 gives -17.03 C vs -17.33 C measured; rate 5 gives -15.27 vs -14.51 C. Coefficient differs between oils: 2.5 for oil C, about 1.65 C per ln unit for oil A.

name: DeepStar supercooling correction for cloud point
equation_text: Correction of about 2 times the cooling rate in F/min (abstract wording); here converted to C: WAT_corrected = WATm + 2.0*rate
fitted_on: DeepStar GoM oils, lab cloud point methods
reported_accuracy: Four methods within 3 F of all-method mean after correction
citation: Monger-McClure, T.G., Tackett, J.E. and Merrill, L.S. (1997). DeepStar comparisons of cloud point measurement and paraffin prediction methods. SPE 38774.
notes: Test: WATm 30 C at 1 C/min gives 32.0 C. Unit conversion: 2 F per (F/min) equals 2.0 C per (C/min). Coutinho and Daridon 2005 report it as equal to the rate in K/min, so k could be 1.0; treat k as uniform 1 to 2.

name: Method detection-threshold offset (generator rule)

inputs.name: wax precipitation slope just below WAT

equation_text: WAT_measured = WATt - f/s - k*rate (assembled from cited facts, not printed as one equation in any source)
fitted_on: Thresholds: Hammami, Ratulowski and Coutinho 2003 (0.01 to 0.1 wt% best methods), Coutinho et al. 2006 (SDS 0.16 to 0.43, filter 1 wt%), Coutinho and Daridon 2005 (viscometry 0.3 to 1 wt%), DSC from memory; slopes from Kruka 1995 via Hammami 2003 (0.4 wt%/C fast, about ten times slower for GoM oils) and Cao 2022 (0.16 to 0.18 max)
reported_accuracy: Not validated as a whole; consistent with same-oil pairs (CPM minus DSC +2 to +10 C, Dabei microscope minus DSC +10 C with s about 0.05 to 0.18)
citation: Assembled by this agent from Hammami et al. (2003), Coutinho and Daridon (2005), Coutinho et al. (2006), Monger-McClure et al. (1997)
notes: Test: WATt 40, s 0.1, DSC f 0.3, k 1, rate 1 gives 36.0 C; CPM f 0.02 at rate 0.5 gives 39.3 C. Precipitation slope near WAT is small for oils with long paraffin tails, making offsets large.

name: WAT from pour point and wax content (gap model, master_v9)
equation_text: WAT - pour = -0.498*wax + 26.5 (OLS on master_v9, n=163, r=-0.41)
fitted_on: master_v9 non-X rows with WAT, pour and wax (163 rows, mixed methods)
reported_accuracy: r = -0.41 for the gap; residual SD large (about 15 C)
notes: Test: pour 0, wax 10 gives 21.5 C; pour 30, wax 25 gives 44.1 C. Use only as a consistency check in the generator (the gap must stay positive, rarely above 55 C).

name: WDT from WAT by method (median offsets, master_v9)
equation_text: WDT = WAT + d; d median 8.0 (CPM), 12.1 (DSC 2 C/min), 6.0 (D8420), 4.8 (rheometer), 8.2 all
fitted_on: 39 master_v9 rows with both WAT and WDT
notes: Test: WAT 30 with d 8.0 gives 38.0 C. Literature: about 15 K DSC and 10 K microscopy (Coutinho and Daridon 2005); 3 to 4 C at 0.01 C/min (Gimzewski and Audley).

name: WAT from wax content (log form, master_v9)
fitted_on: master_v9 non-X rows with wax over 0 (223 rows, mixed methods)
notes: Test: wax 10 gives 32.84 C; wax 2 gives 14.81 C.
